about: The TypeScript plugin's mutant ledger (SEMWS WG4): each row is a fault of split.js or main.js and the test of split.test.js that alone kills it. Run: bun mutants.js [NAME...].

mutants.name: ts-key-by-offset
mutants.rule: A unit is keyed by its declared names, never by its offset (the plan's 'a unit keyed by its position'; row: a key is the declared names).

mutants.name: ts-overloads-apart
mutants.from: if (name !== null && last && last.fn === name && last.open) {
mutants.rule: An overload set is one unit, not two with one key (row: an overload set is one unit).

mutants.name: ts-leading-comment-lost
mutants.rule: The comment above a statement belongs to its unit, not to the unit before (row: a leading comment belongs to its unit).

mutants.name: ts-cut-in-a-comment
mutants.rule: A unit's end never falls inside a comment that spans a line break (row: a leading comment belongs to its unit).

mutants.name: ts-tsx-as-ts
mutants.rule: A .tsx file parses as TSX (row: a .tsx file is parsed as TSX).

mutants.name: ts-module-cut-in-two
mutants.to: const groups = grouped(r.program.body.flatMap((s) => (s.type === "TSModuleDeclaration" && s.body && s.body.body ? s.body.body : [s])));
mutants.rule: A declare module block is one unit, not one a statement (the plan's 'a declare module block cut in two'; row: a declare module block is one unit).

mutants.name: ts-no-members
mutants.rule: Classes, interfaces, enums, objects and imports have members (row: members by name).

mutants.name: ts-duplicate-keys
mutants.rule: A name declared twice (interface merging) keys its later declarations apart (KeysAreUnique on the corpus).

mutants.name: ts-code-after-neighbour
mutants.rule: A statement with no name is not keyed by the unit before it, whose rename would move its key (EditStaysInItsUnit on seeded edits).

mutants.name: ts-sites-empty
mutants.rule: A level-1 plugin asked for Sites answers NotProvided, never an empty list (row: the protocol).
